title: Processing and Characterization of Monodisperse Silicon Colloids
protocol: Set the Variac to 70% power and preheat the brass block to 485 °C.
Clean the titanium reactor and the plug with chloroform and dry in the fumehood.
Place the reactor and the plug into the ante-chamber of the glovebox.
Take three cycles of exhaustion, each lasting at least ten minutes.
Prepare an ice bath in a bucket where the water level is lower than the height of the reactor.
Measure 5.8 ml of n-Hexane and add to the reactor.
Measure 18 μl of trisilane and add to the reactor along with n-Hexane.
Put on the plug and tighten with a wrench immediately after adding reagents.
Remove the reactor from the glovebox and further tighten the plug with a vice and wrench.
Remove the empty reactor from the preheated brass block and place in the loaded reaction vessel.
Change the temperature setting to 425 °C and start the timer.
After 10 min, remove the reactor from the heating block and submerge in an ice bath to quench to room temperature.
Open the reactor with a wrench after cooling to room temperature.
Collect the product using a glass pipette.
Centrifuge the product at 8000 rpm for 5 min to precipitate particles.
Discard the supernatant, redisperse the product in 5 mL of chloroform with sonication, and centrifuge again.
Discard the supernatant, redisperse the particles in chloroform.
Evaporate the solvent from the a-Si:H colloidal suspension by heating it at 120 °C in an oven.
Put dried a-Si:H particles into a chamber.
Create high vacuum within the chamber using a turbo-molecular vacuum pump.
Anneal the chamber with an oven to a temperature between 200 °C and 600 °C for one hour.
Let the chamber cool down slowly (1 °C/min) to room temperature under vacuum environment.
Set up the home-made confocal microscope combined with a spectrometer coupler working in NIR region.
Place a drop of silicon colloid suspension on a glass substrate and wait for the chloroform to evaporate.
Put the glass substrate onto the sample holder of the confocal microscope and focus the sample.
Select a single particle and close the confocal aperture of the setup.
Tune the designed spectrometer coupler of the setup, and optimize the signal-noise ratio.
Measure the spectra once the InGaAs detector is cooled down with liquid nitrogen.
